mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or the rise is <0.25% in magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level indicates weakening labor market strength, which is associated with lower consumer confidence and lower S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month's PAYEMS for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the identified labor weakening period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over the next quarter, it suggests robust business demand outpacing cost pressures, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified imbalance period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the goods price index (not available in the catalog; fallback to HOUST as a supply proxy) coinciding with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests supply-side contraction, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
Note: Since no direct supply series is available, using HOUST as a proxy for output/supply. This is a theoretical fallback for the exercise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 5% while UNRATE rises over the next month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the contraction episode.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of sustained monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be positive as lower rates encourage investment in long-term assets.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in at least 60% of easing episodes (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (not directly observable; fallback to UNRATE as a labor signal) above historical averages coincides with higher consumer sentiment and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the identified labor market loosening period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not directly observable; using GDPC1 as a demand proxy) exceed expectations by 2% or more, it signals strong consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 105% of prior month's value (2% monthly growth)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) during the identified demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) of more than 10% over two months suggests supply disruptions, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >10% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the disruption episode.
